summary: Plan relief shipment documents, exemptions and clearance handoffs through scenario-based humanitarian import preparedness training. Explore the course.
lede: Humanitarian import preparedness training helps logistics, procurement and operations teams plan relief shipments around customs procedures. Participants map clearance steps, check shipment documents and consignee details, plan exemption requests, and coordinate broker and authority follow-up. Scenario exercises help them identify likely bottlenecks, assign escalation responsibilities and prepare an import-readiness action plan, while keeping local procedure confirmation and the limits of legal advice in view.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who prepare or coordinate humanitarian relief imports and need to align programme, procurement, logistics and external clearance work. It suits professionals with operational responsibilities who want to plan for country-specific procedures without treating training as a substitute for local legal advice or customs brokerage.
prerequisites: Prior experience in humanitarian logistics, procurement, programme operations or emergency preparedness is recommended. No coding or specialist software is required. The course supports operational planning and does not replace customs brokerage or country-specific legal advice.
